# The cash sale again, linked by `txn_guid:` alone.
#
# The account-type check went on the spelling that names the split, and
# Q-039 says the two spellings reach the same place — so this one still moved
# the revenue onto the receivable. The check belongs on the split that is about
# to move, not on the words that chose it.
#
# Worse, this arm *regressed*. The size used to be the split's own figure, so a
# CAD income split of −139.00 against a 100.00 USD invoice hit "exceeds invoice
# remaining" and the file was turned away by accident. Reading the size off the
# bank removed that barrier without putting the deliberate one in its place.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming the income account, with the
# revenue still on it.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-03-16
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    txn_guid: "1122aabb3344ccdd5566eeff77880099"
